notes.text: Ivan Demidov is on injured reserve (ankle injury) and has missed the last 17 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Chris Kreider is out (lower-body injury), reported after he played in their last game.
Mike Matheson returned in their last game after missing 6 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Oliver Kapanen is no longer killing penalties: 1% of the team’s shorthanded time in 12 games, down from 33% last season.
Arber Xhekaj has started killing penalties: on the ice for 26% of the team’s shorthanded time in 18 games, up from 6% last season.
Jordan Staal has not dressed for the last 14 games. Mark Jankowski has taken his spot beside Jordan Martinook and Nikolaj Ehlers.

stakes: The Canadiens go in tied for first in the Atlantic with 28 points, the Hurricanes first in the Metropolitan with 32 points.

CAR.head: A big edge for the Hurricanes

story.head: Best vs. best
paras: The Hurricanes won the teams’ first meeting this season, 6-4 in Montréal on Oct 6. The Hurricanes have won three straight, and the Canadiens (12-3-4) beat Boston 5-2 on Nov 12. Two of the league’s best teams meet. The Canadiens played last night, and the Hurricanes are rested. Going in, the Canadiens are second in the Atlantic (tied for fifth in the NHL) and the Hurricanes first in the Metropolitan (tied for first).

The Canadiens’ record (.737) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.563), largely because they’re 7-5 in one-goal games. The Hurricanes’ record (.800) is about what their chances are worth.

The Hurricanes (32nd) and the Canadiens (29th) both give up a lot of dangerous shots. The Canadiens get into more chippy games than almost anyone (2nd) and take more penalties than they draw (30th). On the other side, the Hurricanes take away shots from the point (lowest) and create more chances on the penalty kill than anyone (1st). Carolina has scored 4.10 goals a game, the most in the league, and allowed 2.25, the second fewest. Something has to give when the Canadiens’ shooting runs into the Hurricanes’ defense. Beyond that, the Canes’ power play (6th) could do real damage against the Canadiens’ penalty kill (23rd), though their penalty killers create chances of their own going the other way.

Cole Caufield (12 G / 6 A / 18 P in 19 GP) is tied for the Canadiens’ scoring lead. Lane Hutson (3 G / 15 A / 18 P in 19 GP) shares it. Sebastian Aho (12 G / 16 A / 28 P in 20 GP) leads the Hurricanes in scoring and is tied for seventh in the NHL, with nine points in his last five games. Logan Stankoven (11 G / 9 A / 20 P in 20 GP) is next in line, with eight points in his last five games.

Jakub Dobeš (3-2-2 / .846 SV% in 7 GS) has struggled for Montréal so far, but will likely start. Carolina has two options in net: Pyotr Kochetkov (11-1-0 / .920 SV% in 12 GS) and Brandon Bussi (4-2-2 / .872 SV% in 8 GS). Kochetkov has started seven of their last ten games, so expect him back in net after Bussi got the last one on Nov 12.
At home, Rod Brind'Amour likes to send Robinson, Kotkaniemi and Martinook out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against Kreider, Evans and Anderson.

items.text: The Canadiens are newly without Chris Kreider, and have been without Ivan Demidov and Samuel Montembeault for several games. Jakub Dobeš is expected to start.
Nick Suzuki has a point in five straight games against Carolina.
The Hurricanes have been without Jordan Staal since Oct 10.
Juraj Slafkovský has two goals on chances worth about 6.5 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
